research.title: A tumor transcriptomic atlas across eight decades of life reveals distinct features of early-onset colorectal cancer
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 04 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04771-2 The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer is rising, but whether it is biologically distinct from average-onset disease is unclear. Mapping of the transcriptome of colorectal tumors across the age continuum shows that tumors in younger adults contain more stromal cells.

research.title: Gene editing could replace a lifetime of medication, but there's a catch
research.summary: A single gene-editing treatment could someday protect against heart disease, high cholesterol, and other common conditions for decades, potentially replacing lifelong medications. But scientists warn that permanently altering genes introduces risks that could take years to emerge, making long-term safety a critical challenge.

research.title: Perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy in resectable non-small cell lung cancer: a phase 2 trial
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 04 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04745-4 In a nonrandomized phase 2 trial, patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer received perioperative ivonescimab as monotherapy or with chemotherapy, leading to encouraging pathological response rates in both cohorts, and sustained circulating tumor DNA negativity throughout neoadjuvant therapy may.

research.title: Scientists trick cancer cells into making the drugs that kill them
research.summary: Scientists have developed a promising new cancer-fighting strategy that uses carbon monoxide naturally produced by tumor cells to manufacture powerful drugs inside the cancer cells themselves. Early laboratory experiments suggest the technique could selectively attack cancer while sparing healthy cells, potentially paving the way for safer chemotherapy alternatives.

research.title: A live biotherapeutic product for adult allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients: a partially randomized, placebo-controlled
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 03 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04686-y In a phase 1b study that included an open-label and randomized-controlled cohorts of allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients, treatment with the investigational, cultivated, multi-strain bacterial oral live biotherapeutic product, SER-155, was found to have a similar safety profile to placebo.

research.title: Heterogeneity of microbiome responses to menopausal hormone therapy among perimenopausal women
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 03 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04737-4 In this study, the gut, oral, urinary and vaginocervical microbiomes of women receiving menopausal hormone therapy were studied over 6 months, shedding light on how system metagenomics can inform clinical response and care.

research.title: How smoking sets the stage for lung cancer | Explained
research.summary: Chronic smoke exposure alters lung stem cells and weakens their safety mechanisms and local immune defences, creating a precancerous state, common KRAS and TP53 mutations triggered tumours only in smoke-conditioned tissue, showing how smoking primes cells for cancer
